subsystems.name: Robot unit
subsystems.role: a small mobile robot that can move, sense and manipulate building material.

subsystems.name: Local sensing and positioning
subsystems.role: lets each robot know where it is and what the structure looks like nearby.

subsystems.name: Stigmergic coordination
subsystems.role: robots coordinate indirectly by changing the environment, such as placing a block or leaving a digital marker.

subsystems.name: Material handling
subsystems.role: picks up, carries and places building blocks or repair patches.

subsystems.name: Power and docking
subsystems.role: keeps small robots running without manual battery changes.

subsystems.name: Supervisory interface
subsystems.role: allows a human to set high-level goals without controlling individual robots.

buildSteps.title: Design blocks and robot morphology
buildSteps.detail: Choose block shapes (e.g. 10–20 cm interlocking units) that a small robot can lift and place, and size the robot accordingly.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate robot units
buildSteps.detail: Assemble chassis, motors, gripper, sensors, radio and battery into a robust unit, typically under 30 cm across.

buildSteps.title: Write local control rules
buildSteps.detail: Program each robot with simple if–then rules: if a block is needed here, fetch one; if a gap exists, fill it. No central controller.

buildSteps.title: Simulate the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Test thousands of virtual robots in software to tune rules, avoid deadlocks and check scalability before physical trials.

buildSteps.title: Build a testbed arena
buildSteps.detail: Create a flat, bounded space with a few dozen robots and a supply of blocks to demonstrate basic construction like a wall or pyramid.

buildSteps.title: Scale up the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Increase to hundreds of robots, improving communication range, collision avoidance and task allocation so the group stays coordinated.

buildSteps.title: Trial on infrastructure repair
buildSteps.detail: Deploy the swarm to repair a simple structure, such as filling a crack or assembling a temporary support, in a controlled outdoor setting.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with real surfaces
buildSteps.detail: Develop ways for robots to navigate and attach to vertical or uneven surfaces like bridge piers and building walls.

buildSteps.title: Certify safety and reliability
buildSteps.detail: Test that robots can work safely near people and in public infrastructure, with fail-safes and emergency stop.

prerequisites.why: labs have demonstrated tens of robots building simple structures, but scaling to thousands is unproven.
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and ultra-wideband let robots exchange local information.
small cameras, motors and microcontrollers are mass-produced and cheap.
SLAM works in structured spaces, but robust operation in cluttered, changing construction sites is still hard.
well studied in simulation, yet physical implementation with real materials is limited.
current lithium-ion batteries give only a few hours of operation, limiting continuous work.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of tens of robots building simple structures (e.g. the TERMES project at Harvard, 2014)
pathway.unlocks: proof that stigmergic construction works in the physical world.

pathway.milestone: swarms of hundreds of robots building larger structures in controlled environments
pathway.unlocks: scalability, robustness and faster build times.

pathway.milestone: field trials for infrastructure repair, such as crack sealing or scaffolding assembly
pathway.unlocks: real-world application in construction and maintenance.

pathway.milestone: thousands of robots autonomously building or repairing large infrastructure with minimal human oversight
pathway.unlocks: rapid, low-cost construction and repair of bridges, buildings and pipelines.
